correctness.rationale: Perron vertex-mass identities show lambda(lambda-n+1)>=k, equality iff matching. At lambda>n-1 the Schur complement reduces the upper bound to a weighted singular norm; its Frobenius trace is maximized uniquely by bridge-degree squared sum k^2+k, attained by a rank-one star. The matching quadratic, unique star resolvent root, bounded excess-spectrum limit, and exact n=4,k=3 rational sign evaluations establish every asserted spectral and asymptotic boundary. SIS map monotonicity, union-bound Perron Lyapunov decrease at equality, strict radial subhomogeneity, and sub/supersolution squeezing prove extinction versus globally attracting positive equilibrium. The standalone checker passed 5421 graph configurations and 9 asymptotic checks; these are supplementary finite tests.

originality.rationale: Full primary text of the 2026 motivating SIS threshold-set paper proves only the one-sided local versus global inequality. Closest literature concerning the same two-clique matching/source graphs studies fastest-mixing random-walk conductance, not unnormalized adjacency spectral extrema. A 2026 star/matching spectral supersaturation study uses different Turan multipartite constraints. Targeted published-finding corpus and web queries found no statement subsuming the fixed cross-edge-budget extrema, equality cases, scaling law, or explicit reverse SIS outcomes. Residual risk of an unindexed equivalent spectral graph theorem is material and disclosed.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible specialized spectral-extremal literature could contain an equivalent two-clique fixed-budget theorem; indexed search is not a proof of uniqueness.

The original SIS probability recurrence is a deterministic approximation under a neighbor-independence closure; positive mean-field equilibrium is not indefinite survival of the finite stochastic SIS chain.
The theorem does not cover more than n cross edges, unequal or non-clique communities, heterogeneous rates, or directed and weighted contacts.

value.rationale: The fixed inter-community bridge-budget problem supplies an applied-network structural optimal-design answer absent from local community threshold sets: matching is uniquely least prone and star uniquely most prone by exact threshold, despite identical isolated-community rates. A rigorous k/n scaling window quantifies a nonzero asymptotic difference and a rational n=4 counterexample exhibits genuine extinction versus attracting endemic dynamics for the same infection and recovery probabilities. This is a motivated natural classification with direct mathematical implications, not a renamed eigenvalue computation or a finite table alone.
